items.title: 67460_Sammy Price oral history interview
items.q: Mayo and I became inseparable and we'd go to Chicago and take like Little Brother Montgomery and find him

ctx.x: Right. "Sam Price and His Four Quarters." And Mayo liked me. But I didn't see him any more until I saw him in Chicago years later. And when I saw him in Chicago years later, he said to me...well, this was in '33 I think it was..."If you ever come to New York, look me up." So I didn't have no idea...I didn't realize that he was commuting from New York to Chicago. So I went up to the room and Cow Cow says, "Sam Price!" "Hey He says, /Mayo, I got it! I taught Sam the 'Cow Cow Blues;'" said, "This little kid beat me…

Wheatstraw . As a matter of fact, I used to go... Mayo and I became inseparable and we'd go to Chicago and take like Little Brother Montgomery and find him, get him together, get his songs together and I would get his songs straightened out out in Chicago before we'd get here, so we would save time. Then we'd get a bottle of whiskey and go down the highway and end up at the Woodside Hotel. And the following day we'd go sign the contract, you know, when are you going to leave and all that business, and then I'd go…

you know. They said I could play. But I never said I could play the piano. I never did. So, we went in and we made the "Cow Cow Blues" and after that came a sequence of things...I did "Fetch It To Me," with Don Stovall and those guys...
